newsitem.title: UK: UK supermarket shares rise as investors seek shelter.
newsitem.headline: UK supermarket shares rise as investors seek shelter.

text.p: A further rebound in shares in Safeway PLC and Tesco Plc on Friday was seen as evidence investors are seeking shelter in domestic stocks that have underperformed the broad market in recent months, dealers and strategists said.

In an environment where UK and U.S. interest rates appear poised to rise, investment flows into UK supermarket chain shares has come at the expense of the financial sector, which has been a runaway outperformer so far this year, they said.
On Friday, shares in Safeway closed up nine pence at 362p, while shares in Tesco closed up one penny at 340p. It was the third straight day the shares rose, even as the broad market tumbled.
"It's a defensive play," said one marketmaker of this week's rebound in food retailer stocks.
Since January, shares in big food retailers have been dogged by worries about price wars.

Shares in Tesco, the biggest supermarket chain in terms of market capitalisation, have lagged the FTSE All-Share index by about 10 percent during the past three months, according to Reuters Securities 3000.
Safeway shares have underperformed the All-Share by a stunning 18 percent since mid-January, Reuters Securities 3000 data show.
But some strategists questioned whether this week's rotation is sustainable.
"I think this is a short-term trend that's likely to reverse later in the year," said Bob Semple, UK equity strategist with NatWest Securities.
He said inflation isn't likely to heat up enough to allow grocers to raise prices and bolster profit margins.
Semple figures investors will use the recent decline in bank shares as a buying opportunity.
He was forecasting renewed strength in the bank sector after the UK election on May 1, despite widespread expectations for a UK interest rate increase.
Bank analysts said it would take an increase of one to 1.5 percent before it would make an impact on banks' profits.

By Thursday's close, the UK bank sector had outperformed the FTSE All-Share index by 10 percent, even after a sharp wave of profit-taking sparked by interest rate concerns during the past week, according to Reuters Securities 3000.
At their peak, UK bank shares had outperformed the All-Share by 17 percent during the previous six months.
Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc slid 13-1/2p to 673. Shares in Lloyds TSB Group eased 10p to 466-1/2p, while shares in Royal Bank of Scotland tumbled 12-1/2p to 517-1/2.
